results.title: KV Cache Quantization vLLM Setup: KIVI's INT2 Method (2026) | Spheron Blog
results.content: KIVI's own throughput and memory experiments were run on a single NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU, per the paper. That's the same GPU class you'd provision to reproduce these numbers directly, since matching the paper's hardware means matching its memory bandwidth and capacity ceiling rather than approximating it on a different card. Whatever headroom KIVI frees up in the KV cache translates directly into either a longer context window per sequence or more concurrent sequences in the same batch: the two [...] CoQA holds up close to fp16 on both models, roughly a single point of degradation. GSM8K is more sensitive on Mistral-7B specifically, a 2.35-point drop, which is worth flagging if your workload leans on multi-step arithmetic or chain-of-thought reasoning rather than retrieval-style QA. The pattern matches what you'd expect from any aggressive KV cache compression: tasks that depend on precise intermediate reasoning steps propagated through a long context are more exposed to cache-quantization [...] The vLLM blog's own benchmarking reports FP8 KV cache reducing per-token cache cost to as low as 54% of the BF16 baseline in the best cases. That's roughly half the memory and it costs you nothing operationally: FP8 stays inside vLLM's PagedAttention scheduler, continuous batching, and everything else the engine already does well.

results.content:
KIVI is a new plug-and-play 2bit KV cache quantization algorithm without any fine-tuning. This algorithm optimizes memory usage by quantizing the key cache per-channel and the value cache per-token to 2bit. KIVI's hardware-friendly design allows LLMs like Llama-2, Falcon, and Mistral to maintain comparable quality levels while reducing peak memory usage by 2.6 times. This enables up to 4 times larger batch sizes and significantly increases throughput by 2.35 to 3.47 times in real LLM inference [...] real LLM inference workloads, effectively addressing the bottleneck issues in speed and memory usage. results.content:
KIVI

The KIVI paper highlights around 2.6x lower peak memory including weights, up to 4x larger batch size, and 2.35x–3.47x throughput gains on real inference workloads.

## What changes between the two methods

TurboQuant and KIVI both target KV cache memory, but they optimize for different points on the accuracy, complexity, and compression tradeoff curve. TurboQuant adds more math to reduce distortion; KIVI keeps the method simpler and more directly tied to 2-bit cache compression. [...] ## Which one looks stronger on paper

TurboQuant

### TurboQuant looks stronger if quality retention is the priority

Google's paper emphasizes low-distortion inner-product estimation, long-context quality, and benchmark parity near the 3 to 4-bit operating range.

KIVI

### KIVI looks stronger if simplicity and 2-bit cache reduction are the priority

KIVI is easier to reason about as a KV-only quantization baseline and is commonly referenced when teams want a direct 2-bit comparison point. [...] KIVI

Distribution-aware KV quantization: per-channel quantization for keys and per-token quantization for values.
